profile.reading: Data Foundry is a privately held Texas colocation operator. This facility, branded Houston 2 on the operator's own site, sits at 660 Greens Parkway, Houston, Texas 77067, near George Bush Intercontinental Airport in Harris County, and is the only Houston facility named on Data Foundry's current data centers index page. The operator's own materials describe the building as 350,000 square feet on an 18-acre campus, with dual underground utility feeds, 2.25 MW Cummins diesel backup generators, and N+1 to 2N power redundancy options depending on customer tier, and cite 60 MW of power capacity available to the site; that 60 MW figure describes utility power access rather than a certified critical-IT-load rating, so it is not recorded here as critical_it_mw. Data Foundry has operated in Texas for more than two decades, with its current portfolio concentrated in Austin (three facilities: Data Foundry 00/Austin 1, Data Foundry 01, and Data Foundry 02, all tracked separately elsewhere in this registry) and this single Houston facility; unlike larger REIT-owned or private-equity-backed operators in this registry, Data Foundry remains an independent Texas company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's power and redundancy details are sourced solely to the operator's own published materials. No year-opened date or independently audited MW figure was located for this facility in sourcing reachable this session. The George Bush Intercontinental Airport-adjacent Greens Point/North Houston submarket where this facility sits has become a secondary hub for enterprise and disaster-recovery colocation demand outside Houston's energy-corridor core, drawing customers seeking geographic diversification from the state's primary Dallas and Austin data center clusters. Data Foundry markets its Houston presence specifically toward disaster-recovery and business-continuity customers headquartered elsewhere in Texas, citing distance-based diversity from its Austin facilities as a selling point, per the operator's own materials reviewed this session.

reading.body:
Data Foundry's Houston facility holds 60 MW of colocation capacity on a 350,000 square foot campus, but the operator does not publicly disclose how much is currently committed to AI workloads.

The facility sits near George Bush Intercontinental Airport in Harris County with dual underground utility feeds and 2.25 MW of backup generation offering N+1 to 2N redundancy. This infrastructure pattern reflects colocation operator standards rather than the single-customer, ultra-high-density builds increasingly favored by large AI labs. Data Foundry markets space to multiple customers across sectors, not exclusively to AI.

The 60 MW capacity ceiling matters for AI scaling only if occupied by inference, training, or supporting infrastructure. Colocation operators typically run at partial utilization and mix workloads. Without disclosed critical IT load figures or customer composition data, the facility's actual contribution to AI compute capacity remains opaque. The power is available to Houston's grid. Whether it serves AI, traditional enterprise, or other uses determines its relevance to compute constraints on AI growth.
